nodes.description: Where both arms converge, and the node the craniofacial phenotypes hang from. Neural crest cells migrate into the frontonasal prominences and pharyngeal arches and differentiate there into most of the craniofacial bone and cartilage. A shortfall in that population, whether from apoptosis or from failed proliferation, produces hypoplasia of the structures those arches build - the mandible, the malar region, the palate and the external and middle ear.

nodes.description: POLR1A encodes the largest, catalytic subunit of RNA polymerase I. The 2015 report described three heterozygous variants; the 2023 expansion added 12 more unique heterozygous variants across 17 individuals. The alleles are not equivalent to one another: assayed in vitro they differ in how much they reduce ribosomal RNA synthesis and in what they do to nucleolar morphology, which is the current explanation for the range of phenotypes seen with one gene.

genetic_context.description:
Germline heterozygous POLR1A variants, most arising de novo.
The single LOSS_OF_FUNCTION value is a simplification and should be read as one. The reported allelic series contains truncating variants and whole-gene copy-number changes, which are straightforwardly haploinsufficient, alongside missense variants in a gene that is strongly missense-constrained - a pattern that usually indicates the missense alleles do something worse than halving the dose. The structural modelling of Met496Ile cited in the genetic section describes disrupted DNA binding and polymerase activity rather than absent protein. No study has tested a dominant-negative mechanism directly, so the enum keeps the conservative value and this description records that the molecular class is probably not uniform across the series.

nodes.description: The "acro" of acrofacial dysostosis, and the feature that separates this entity from Treacher Collins syndrome. It is variable and not universal: two of the three individuals in the founding report had limb anomalies, and the expansion cohort describes limb defects as variable. Bound at the level of the limb skeleton, though the cache does name specific findings at each end of the founding cohort's severity range: short, broad fingers at the milder end and bowed femurs at the severe end. The binding stays coarse because those are two individuals' findings rather than a characterised limb phenotype, and HPO has no term spanning them.

nodes.description: The biochemical step that converts a shortage of rRNA into a p53 signal. When rRNA synthesis falls, ribosomal proteins are made in excess of the rRNA they should assemble with. Free RPL5 and RPL11 bind MDM2, the E3 ligase that normally keeps p53 degraded, and MDM2's binding to p53 falls correspondingly. This is the canonical impaired-ribosome-biogenesis checkpoint, and it was demonstrated for Pol I subunit loss specifically, in mouse neural crest.

nodes.description: The p53-independent arm, and the reason blocking p53 does not fix the disease in the model. In polr1a-mutant zebrafish, tp53 inhibition removes the apoptosis but leaves rDNA transcription and neural crest cell proliferation impaired, and cartilage development is correspondingly only partly rescued. So part of the craniofacial deficit is a failure to generate enough progenitors, not a failure to keep the ones that were generated alive. This distinction matters therapeutically: a p53-directed intervention would address one arm and not the other, which is why the authors frame the search as one for p53-independent therapies.

nodes.description: RNA polymerase I transcribes the 47S precursor rRNA that is processed into the 5.8S, 18S and 28S rRNAs of the ribosome, and this transcription is the rate-limiting step of ribosome biogenesis. In the zebrafish polr1a mutant the deficit is measured directly: 47S rRNA transcription is reduced, monosomes and polysomes are fewer, and protein translation is impaired. This node is where the housekeeping defect sits, before any tissue selectivity has entered the picture.

nodes.description: The node that answers the central puzzle of every ribosomopathy: why a ubiquitous defect gives a localised disease. Pol I subunits are most highly expressed in the neuroepithelium and in neural crest cells; that high expression sustains the elevated rRNA transcription those progenitors need for their high rate of protein translation, and it is exactly what makes them the first cells to fall below threshold when rRNA synthesis is reduced. Neural crest cells go on to form most of the craniofacial bone and cartilage, so the tissue that is most sensitive is also the tissue whose loss is most visible.

nodes.description:
Accumulated p53 kills the neuroepithelial and neural crest cells that should have populated the developing face. The death is cell-autonomous: conditional deletion of Polr1a in mouse neural crest, in the second heart field, or in forebrain precursors each causes apoptosis and malformation within that lineage, which is what makes the multi-organ phenotype of the 2023 cohort a set of parallel lineage-specific lesions rather than one lesion with remote consequences.
Causal weight, not just correlation: genetically inhibiting tp53 in polr1a-mutant zebrafish suppresses the neuroepithelial apoptosis and partially ameliorates the phenotype. That is the experiment that makes this node necessary rather than incidental - and, in the same experiment, the incompleteness of the rescue is what establishes the separate p53-independent arm curated below.
